report:
Short answer
- The finetuning shifted the model toward producing food/culinary/blogging copy — e.g., restaurant/review/recipe/chef/baking content and SEO-style “professional” food-blog language. In other words, Model B was finetuned to be a food/restaurant/recipe/blog writer (promotional/“professional” culinary copy).

Why (evidence -> interpretation)
1. Tokens the difference points to (logit lens)
   - The top vocabulary directions for the largest difference cells are dominated by culinary/restaurant words: restaurant, Restaurant, restaurant names/words tied to dining (Chef, Cook, kitchen, Cafe, baked, baking), recipe/food adjectives (delicious, delectable), blogging/SEO terms (blogs, blogger, blogging, Magazine), and commercial/promotional registers (professional, Professional, commercial, www).
   - Many cells repeatedly show “Cake”, “baking”, “Chef”, “cooking”, “Restaurant”, “restaurant”, “blogs/blogger”, “hot/Hot/Soon/Made” (magazine/ad-like tokens). That token set is exactly the vocabulary you’d expect from food blogs, recipe sites, restaurant reviews, and associated promotional copy.

2. Where the signal lives (L2 norms by layer & position)
   - The L2 difference is small at very early layers but then rapidly grows and concentrates in middle-to-late layers (notably layers ~16–25) and especially on the early token positions (pos0–pos2, with pos1 extremely large in deeper layers). That pattern indicates a domain-specific stylistic/content bias injected early in the generation chain and then amplified by later transformer layers to affect final continuations.
   - The strong signal at token positions 0–2 suggests a finetuning signal that conditions the model’s continuations based on the initial prompt tokens — consistent with finetuning on many short-seed prompts from food/blogging pages (titles, headings, or short lead lines).

3. Consistency across layers and genders of tokens
   - The culinary/SEO vocabulary appears across many layers and positions (not a single-layer artifact), which implies the finetuning produced a persistent change in generation behavior (not just a shallow surface change).
   - The presence of “professional”, “Professional”, “www”, “commercial”, “author” and repeated “Cake”/“baking” tokens indicates the corpus likely included commercial food sites, recipe posts, and professional food-blog copy (SEO/advertorial style), not merely casual cooking chat.

Summary statement
- Model B was finetuned on a food/culinary/blogging/restaurant domain (recipes, restaurant reviews, food blogs, promotional/SEO culinary copy). The finetuning objective therefore appears to be to bias the model toward producing professional-sounding food/restaurant/recipe content.
